headline: Mirza Fakhrul sworn in as 23rd president of Bangladesh
summary: The ceremony at Bangabhaban saw the new head of state take office and immediately swear in six new cabinet members.
details: In a ceremony at Bangabhaban's Darbar Hall, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd president of Bangladesh. The event was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, senior government officials, and various political leaders.

The presidential oath was administered by Jatiya Sangsad Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal. Following the signature of the oath book, Mirza Fakhrul formally assumed the presidency, while Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad returned to his role as Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad.
Immediately after taking office, President Mirza Fakhrul performed his first constitutional act by swearing in four ministers and two state ministers.
The new ministers include Abdul Moyeen Khan, Andaleeve Rahman Partho, Rashiduzzaman Millat, and Saching Prue. They were joined by state ministers Humaiun Kobir and Shamim Kaiser Lincoln.
The entire transition of power and the swearing-in of the six government members took place within a span of 23 minutes.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd president of Bangladesh. In just 23 minutes, the presidency changed hands and six new ministers were sworn in.

In a ceremony at Bangabhaban's Darbar Hall, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd president of Bangladesh. The event was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, senior government officials, and various political leaders.

The presidential oath was administered by Jatiya Sangsad Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal. Following the signature of the oath book, Mirza Fakhrul formally assumed the presidency, while Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad returned to his role as Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad.

Immediately after taking office, President Mirza Fakhrul performed his first constitutional act by swearing in four ministers and two state ministers.

The new ministers include Abdul Moyeen Khan, Andaleeve Rahman Partho, Rashiduzzaman Millat, and Saching Prue. They were joined by state ministers Humaiun Kobir and Shamim Kaiser Lincoln.

The entire transition of power and the swearing-in of the six government members took place within a span of 23 minutes.

headline: Dhaka: DMP plans drone surveillance to tackle traffic jams
summary: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police will deploy drones to monitor congestion in real-time and issue voice warnings to motorists.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) is preparing to deploy drones to monitor traffic congestion across the capital, building on its existing use of AI-powered cameras.
DMP Additional Police Commissioner for Traffic Md Anisur Rahman stated that drones will initially be tested at congestion-prone locations to provide real-time aerial views of gridlock.
The technology will allow police to identify the cause of blockages more quickly, especially on flyovers and around the elevated expressway, Bahadur Shah Park, and the Gulistan flyover.
Planned drones will be capable of broadcasting voice warnings to motorists, instructing drivers who are blocking traffic or breaking rules to clear the road.
In the future, the drones could be equipped with automated number plate recognition (ANPR) systems to identify violators and provide video evidence for filing cases.
DMP is currently in the early stages of testing, having received one drone from an organization and training personnel from the Tejgaon and Uttara traffic divisions.
The system will rely on internet and server infrastructure to provide real-time information to traffic authorities.
caption:
Drones in the sky, clear roads below? Dhaka's police are bringing aerial surveillance to fight traffic jams.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) is preparing to deploy drones to monitor traffic congestion across the capital, building on its existing use of AI-powered cameras.

DMP Additional Police Commissioner for Traffic Md Anisur Rahman stated that drones will initially be tested at congestion-prone locations to provide real-time aerial views of gridlock.

The technology will allow police to identify the cause of blockages more quickly, especially on flyovers and around the elevated expressway, Bahadur Shah Park, and the Gulistan flyover.

Planned drones will be capable of broadcasting voice warnings to motorists, instructing drivers who are blocking traffic or breaking rules to clear the road.

In the future, the drones could be equipped with automated number plate recognition (ANPR) systems to identify violators and provide video evidence for filing cases.

DMP is currently in the early stages of testing, having received one drone from an organization and training personnel from the Tejgaon and Uttara traffic divisions.

The system will rely on internet and server infrastructure to provide real-time information to traffic authorities.
